summary:
Garage door opener acting up in Miami? Before you shop for a new one, rule out the simple causes in ten minutes. Check the outlet and breaker, clean and realign the safety sensors near the floor, and try a fresh remote battery. Then pull the release cord and lift the door by hand. If it feels heavy or won't stay put halfway, the springs or tracks need attention, and a new motor won't fix that.

Our latest guide also explains the signs an opener has really reached the end, what the Consumer Product Safety Commission says about auto-reverse and sensors, and what to look for in a replacement, from drive type to storm battery backup. Miami humidity and salt air are hard on opener electronics, so know what you're dealing with before you buy.
